data.narrative:
Cellino, a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Nabiha Saklayen and Marinna Madrid, has raised approximately $125M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 3 public companies (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private biotech firms, though narrow peer matching within identical stage and valuation tier proved insufficient for direct median comparison.

Only one valuation method yielded a quantifiable result. Stage-progression analysis, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $125M capital base, implies a valuation of $250M. This multiplier reflects expected value creation and dilution patterns observed across early-stage biotech financings. Peer-median anchoring could not be applied: while 7 same-sector peers exist, none met the three-datapoint threshold required for robust cohort analysis when filtered by stage and tier. Public-comp P/S anchoring is similarly inapplicable; the Biotech & Health sector median trades at 7.4x revenue across the 3 public comparables, but Cellino's revenue is not disclosed, precluding multiple application.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $212M to $288M, centered at $250M. This range reflects reasonable variance around the stage-progression output but remains constrained by reliance on a single applicable method. Key uncertainties include Cellino's actual revenue or revenue run-rate, which would unlock public-comp anchoring, and the availability of more precisely matched private-stage peers. The median valuation carries material model risk given the narrow methodological foundation.
